summary: # Animation Tools Tutorial Welcome to the quick start tutorial on animation tools. In this guide, we will explore the features of the animation editor, including how to record and adjust animations, load avatars, and manage garment simulations. ## Animation Editor Overview Clicking the arrow at the very bottom of the interface will open and close the animation editor. The animation editor interface is mainly divided into three parts: 1. **Animation Editor Toolbar** Located at the top left, the toolbar contains tools to record, play, and edit animations or capture video. Additionally, you can set various settings here. 2. **Animation Timeline** Below the toolbar, the animation timeline displays animation layers and keyframes for avatar or garment animations. 3. **Quick Menu** On the right side of the editor, the quick menu allows for fast access to set animation options. ## Loading Avatars ### Avatar Options On the right, you can load the avatar. When loading the avatar, you can choose to directly use the default avatar from the library window or import a model created in another 3D software. You can also load your device here and carry out available lighting adjustments. ### Draping Garments To drape a garment on the avatar in T-pose, first load a motion file from the avatar's motion folder. In the "Open Motion" dialog, toggle on "Move Avatar and Garment to Start Position" to help position garments close to the avatar where the animation starts. Transition animations are created in the animation timeline, allowing the avatar's pose to change smoothly. ## Importing Avatars with Animation To import an avatar with animation, go to the Main Menu, select **File** > **Import**, and choose the file format you wish to import. Supported formats include FBX, Alembic, or USD. In the pop-up window, set the object type as "Avatar" and toggle on the "Joint Animations" tab. This allows for importing the avatar with animation and caching animation. ### Adjusting Import Settings You can set the scale and axis conversion as desired. Additionally, toggle on the option to move the garment to the start position to prepare for recording the animation. ## Using Morph Targets If the avatar is not in T-pose or A-pose where the animation starts, you may use a morph target to fit the garment to the posed avatar. Export the avatar at the start frame as an OBJ file. Import the T-pose or A-pose avatar through the OBJ file and drape the garment on it. ### Setting Up Morph Targets Toggle on "Automatically Add Arrangement Points" to simplify arranging and draping garments. Once garments are draped well on the avatar, use the morph target to change the avatar's pose. Set the morphing frame count to define the duration of the transition frames; a higher count will result in a longer but more stable pose transition. ## Recording Animation ### Preparing for Recording Load the avatar with animation to replace the static avatar. Adjust animation settings before recording, including frame rates. You can toggle to other common FPS or set it manually. When simulating garments on a static avatar, we typically use normal simulation assets; however, for recordings, it's recommended to use "Animation Stable." Recording again with this setting will provide more accurate results. ### Simulation Quality You can set simulation quality as custom and input desired values. The higher the value, the better the simulation quality, though it may take more time to record. For "Animation Stable" assets, the recommended simulation quality is 5. ## Additional Recording Tips 1. **Pattern Layer Adjustment** Set the pattern layer back to zero before recording to prevent patterns from intersecting. 2. **Using Pins** To prevent garments from slipping, use the pin tool to pin the pattern to the avatar. 3. **Avoiding Animation Deletion** Be cautious when taking steps that may alter meshes or vertices, as this can delete the animation. 4. **Adding Keys** Add keys for pins or wind controllers to create various simulation effects. Right-click on the time slider line to add a pin key. ## Playback and Layer Management ### Playing Animation Click "Play" to play the animation. Use the playback controls to navigate through the animation, including moving to the beginning or end, stepping one frame back or forward, and activating loop playback. ### Managing Animation Layers Animation layers can be reordered, locked, or hidden. To adjust keyframes, you can delete individual keyframes or select a range to delete. Use the create keyframe button or the S hotkey to key patterns in place. ## Exporting Animation After recording, you can export the animation through **File** > **Export** and select the desired file type. To export specific garments, hide unwanted items by selecting them and pressing SHIFT+Q before exporting. Thank you for watching! See you next time!
